chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yasin al-Darir from Hariz from one who narrated to him from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the value of the quumri, the zanj, the suman, the sparrow, and the nightingale. He said, 'Its value. And if the person in ihram kills it within the sanctuary, upon him is double its value, and there is no dam (blood sacrifice) upon him.' And we have clarified in what preceded that doubling is only required for that which is less than the badanah (cow). When it reaches it, more than it is not required, and to add clarity to that is what he narrated:

key_terms.الزِّنْجِيِّ: A type of small bird (possibly a finch or sparrow)
key_terms.السُّمَانَ: A type of small bird (possibly a lark)
key_terms.الْبَدَنَةِ: A mature female camel used for sacrifice
key_terms.الْقُمْرِِيُّ: A type of small bird (quail or similar)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood sacrifice (usually a camel, cow, or sheep)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for killing small birds while in ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that the penalty for killing small birds (such as the quail or sparrow) while in ihram is limited to double their market value (*qimah*), explicitly excluding the obligation of a blood sacrifice (*dam*). The text further contextualizes this by referencing the principle that the penalty scales with the animal's size, ensuring that smaller creatures do not incur a penalty exceeding that of a *badanah* (year-old camel), thereby demonstrating the juristic precision in distinguishing between minor infractions and major sacrificial requirements.
